// diagnostic

E2305

A declared `View<T>` would outlive an owner, or sema cannot stabilize a public owner set for each declared view slot. Read-only views entering non-view owning slots materialize by default; `copies: .Explicit` restores the refusal.

What

A declared `View<T>` would outlive an owner, or sema cannot stabilize a public owner set for each declared view slot. Read-only views entering non-view owning slots materialize by default; `copies: .Explicit` restores the refusal.

Why

Each declared view slot keeps a bounded set of possible receiver, parameter, or static sources through every return path, call, generic instantiation, aggregate projection, function value, lambda, and trait implementation. Every possible owner must stay live; a consumed (`^`) parameter or receiver is freed when the function returns, so it never owns a returned view.

Fix

Keep every possible owner alive (take a returned view's source as a read or `&` parameter, not `^`), preserve the declared view boundary, or remove `copies: .Explicit` / write `view.copy()` when an owning destination is intended.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E2305: tests/ui/nested_payload_view_escape.stderr.

Error [E2305]: Returned view escapes its declared `from` clause
  --> tests/ui/nested_payload_view_escape.jet:7:42
    |
  7 | fn head(packet: Packet, spare: [Int]) -> View<Int> from spare {
    |                                          ^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Every return path's owners must stay inside the sources named after `from`
 Fix: Widen the `from` clause, or stop returning a view from that owner
